report.summary: Chunk 3 of daedalus/spine/bootstrap.py defines gate_parse() and gate_discrimination() with detailed docstring claims about receipt validation, revision clause fix, and count sanity bounds.
risks: line 292 | high | Receipt has no integrity protection; any write to runs/spine/ can forge a receipt naming current HEAD. | Code comment explicitly acknowledges this; no fix intended in this chunk.
line 260 | medium | `pytest_gate_argv` imported from `daedalus.spine.attempt`; if that module is missing, gate_parse will fail at runtime. | Verify existence of that module in the repository.

line 267 | medium | `gate_discrimination` resolves HEAD via `_head_sha` from `daedalus.spine.picker`; if that import fails, head becomes None and function refuses. | Confirm that `_head_sha` exists and behaves as described.
todos: Ensure `_head_sha` in `daedalus.spine.picker` is robust and returns None only on failure.
Document the integrity protection decision for receipts.

handoff.purpose: Define gate_parse() and gate_discrimination() functions for receipt validation and discrimination.

symbols.name: gate_parse
symbols.note: Parses a raw gate receipt dictionary, validating argv, gate_paths, and scope. For receipts, checks argv matches production pytest argv.

symbols.name: gate_discrimination
symbols.note: Reads and validates a discrimination receipt from disk, returning a GateDiscrimination object. Resolves HEAD if not provided, fails on unreachable revision.

claims.text: A receipt only counts when it is present, parseable, measured against THE CURRENT REVISION, internally consistent, clean on every critical class, and bound to the exact gate being authorised.
claims.why: The chunk implements parsing and revision checking, but references to 'clean on every critical class' and 'bound to the exact gate' are not verifiable in this code alone.

claims.text: The revision clause is the same doctrine the map and inventory sources follow: a measurement of a tree that no longer exists is not a measurement of this one.
claims.why: References to 'map and inventory sources' are outside this chunk.

claims.text: TWO OF THESE SIX WERE PROSE UNTIL AN AUDIT FOUND THEM, and both let a forged promotion through: * The revision clause failed OPEN when HEAD could not be read. ... head is now resolved here when not supplied, and an unresolvable revision REFUSES.
claims.why: Lines 297-307 show that if head is None, it is resolved via _head_sha; if resolution fails (head is falsy), the function returns GateDiscrimination(False, ...) refusing the receipt.

claims.text: * No sanity bound on the counts. ... A rate is now rejected unless 0 <= killed <= planted.
claims.why: No code in this chunk validates kill counts; that logic likely exists elsewhere (e.g., in a function that computes kill rate).

claims.text: Still NOT defended, and deliberately named rather than quietly left: the receipt has no integrity protection.
claims.why: No cryptographic signature or integrity check is present in this chunk; the code simply reads and parses the receipt file.

observations.what: gate_parse performs validation of argv, paths, and scope, including checking for NUL bytes and duplicates.
gate_parse imports pytest_gate_argv from daedalus.spine.attempt when receipt is True, and compares argv against expected_argv.
gate_discrimination resolves HEAD via _head_sha from daedalus.spine.picker; if head is None after resolution, the function returns False.
The function gate_discrimination returns GateDiscrimination(False, ...) for various failure modes (no head, no file, unreadable, not an object, state not 'measured').
